title: BBAL: A Bidirectional Block Floating Point-Based Quantisation Accelerator for Large Language Models
problem: LLM deployment on edge devices faces memory and computational constraints; Block Floating Point (BFP) quantization loses small and moderate values because all data align to maximum exponent, degrading LLM accuracy.
motivation: Edge deployment of LLMs requires aggressive quantization; BFP promises lower overhead than FP but suffers quantization error from outlier-driven exponent alignment.
method: BBAL improves Block Floating Point quantization—a technique that compresses numbers by fitting them all to one shared scale—by making the scale selection smarter. Instead of simply using the maximum value's scale (which causes small numbers to lose precision), the bidirectional approach selects the scale by considering both extremes, resulting in better overall accuracy. The system uses a processing element array (a bank of specialized circuits) optimized for this bidirectional quantization, along with an efficient circuit for the nonlinear math operations that language models need. This enables accurate low-bit inference (very few bits per number) on edge accelerators—small, power-efficient devices.
key_novelty: Selecting the Block Floating Point scale bidirectionally (considering both extremes rather than just the maximum) reduces quantization errors caused by outliers, enabling practical hardware acceleration for language models.
contributions: Bidirectional Block Floating Point (BBFP) data format reducing quantization error
BBAL full-stack accelerator architecture with BBFP processing elements
Cost-effective nonlinear computation unit for low-precision arithmetic
22% accuracy improvement vs outlier-aware accelerators; 40% efficiency gain vs standard BFP
primary_theme: Bidirectional BFP quantization for low-precision LLM inference
